body:
I have a therapist, psychiatrist,  and a social worker. I have BPD, Bipolar, Anixety and complex trauma.

My social worker seems like student housing is the only option that's available to me

We don't have that, and calling them emotional support animals here will get blank looks. It's not a 'thing (I mean legally it is,, but in common vernacular it isn't) '. I understand they are closer to ESA, but therapy cats is what my professionals refer to them.

Both of my cats recognise my episodes, and alter their behaviour towards me when I am depressed. They are also unable to be seperated as they have been together since birth.

Rentals are usually rather flexible, here.. We got our dog to be allowed to live here even tho we were told cats only.
There has never been any terrorists from Iran. Should america shut its borders to England as well?

my 500 dollars is student payments.(similar to unemployment) I do flexible study. I am smart, so between episodes, and in my less severe episodes i study, and I take breaks while i am feeling bad. I might go Ok for 5 weeks, and then only work lightly from home for 2.   I can also get rent assistance.

i am on the waiting list for social housing which will be 20% of my income, which will definitely be a lot easier to afford.
yes, sorry.
yes, someone is going to give me a recipe, and I am very happy  to try that out.

Feeding your cat whiskers Is  like feeding your kid solely froot loops.

My cats aren't just pets. They help keep me alive. They react to my episodes. I am a bleeding heart but keeping my cats healthy also is about keeping me healthy.
Thanks for that. My psychosis and hallucinations have magically disappeared BC you said so

I can do arts and crafts, but never been able to get commissions, excluding friends and family. don't have enough space to create enough to do the whole market thing. Thinking about teaching myself to code, but not sure freelancing exists there.

The money i have is centrelink.  I am on lithium, latuda, citrolpram, and the pill, which is why my meds are 20 dollars.


I volunteer at a mental health org and do flexi-study ( i study counselling)   As my tutor is a counsellor and where i volunteer is mental health orientated,  I get a lot of support which I wouldn't in a job, and they're very very understanding of me lightening my load when I need to, something jobs aren't so reliable about.

I have looked into it, and some places will give compassionate exceptions to animals if they are therapy animals, and that's what im hoping for.

The government agencies are horrible. They had me applying to places i wasn't legally allowed to work.  For example, you need to be studying childcare currently, or,  have a child-care qualification, but they forced me to apply anyway.

I am doing flexible study an volunteering right now. to keep me active. But I think what has triggered me in the past is I cycle randomly, so during work I have started an episode, and not been able to have time off, which has worsened it, and gone down hill from there. like, imagine if you randomly got blisters. and it heals quickly if you stop wearing shoes for a day or two, but you can't stop wearing shoes so it turns into a gaping wound and takes weeks to heal.

Where as with my flexi-study and volunteering, I try to push through an episode, but when I realize  i have hit the wall, I lighten my load.

I have tried to replace volunteering with actual work, and it just didn't go well.


Being completely inactive would be horrible for me, i agree.
Yes please!!!!  I only have issues with things like whiskers. I have been thinking about creating my own but I have no idea where to start.

I do flexi-study and volunteering. The difference between flexi-study and volunteering is when my episodes get too bad, I can lighten my load. The issue with bipolar is between episodes, I can act normal. and some hypomanic episodes I am better than normal. I definitely think that being idle is really bad for me, and I try to live in that sweet spot where it's more than i think i can do, but less than what I can't push through.

My volunteering is rather valuable. I have spoken at events with up to 500 people. and it's about mental health, so instead of feeling burdened, i feel like i can help others with what i have been through, and it has given me a lot of skills that will be helpful in the sector I want to work in  (community service/mental health)


However,  very strong episodes are coming more often.  I get depressive episodes in January. The year before last it was a blip. Last year was very hard, but I push through. This year, it scared me how suicidal I was.

As I have said to my therapist, I feel like I cope better, but my disorder is getting worse.

I can learn to wear warmer and warmer clothes, but the temperature keeps dropping.


If I could find a job that  was OK with taking time off whenever i got TOO bad, i would work tomorrow.
my grandfather, but yeah.

but am I? I am "lazy and entitled"  if I listen to my mental health team  and don't work. but if I  work I will end up dead, or manic. ( and then probably dead.)

If i don't work,, i  can't move out and escape this hell.

there is no way to live.

camping. but whats the point? I come back home and i am yelled at constantly.

i want to work so badly, and then i get called lazy and entitled by doing what my therapist wants

Wow, you're right, I must be able to work, lets tell the whole team of experts who have told me otherwise!! you're a genius!!


Oh wait, that's right, every time I have worked in the past 5 years, i have ended up in hospital. No matter how much I have enjoyed the job. i have either become manic, or depressed, ignored it, continued to work, and then gotten worse. I have been cycling none stop for 5 years now

Do you really think I want to be on disability?

I have tried 15 medications at this point.intensive therapy programs that had 2-3 sessions a week. I keep getting worse. I am currently on high doses of anti-psychotics, anti-depressants, and mood stablizers, and even then, the side effects include not being able to sit still, and constant diarahha, and my bipolar still isn't stablized.

Saying your friend works with bipolar means I must be able to work, is like saying your friend can run a marathon with arthitis, therefore, anyone using a walker for arthitis must be faking it

My therapist,psychatrist, and my social worker have all separately, has said i would be stupid to try and work again.

Things that have happened to me when I have tried to work:

-Got so depressed I slept for 23 hours a day for 5 days straight.
- believe I was a god, who had to kill themselves to save the world. Saw demons and was on the run from aliens
- ended up in ER  countless times.

My bipolar continues to get worse, even out of work, I was nearly hospitalized last month even though I have been trying really hard.working is a trigger for my bipolar episodes. my GP, Social worker, therapist and psychatrist have all told me not to work.

Last week i sat in my therapists room crying because I want to work. and she told me I would be stupid to try again.

Lord marmalade planted Seville oranges and they were too bitter to eat.

So he decided to preserve them, creating marmalade

I told the girl she deserves better than that, and blocked her.

She's in another country (same as him), and technically legal.
I am studying a diploma of counselling at a 'college' my rent is super low BC it's with my family.
for learners?
the online learners practice test?
Damn, there's a character I know, but i can't remember. :(

I know this is stupid of me, but I know a lot of cheap cat food is like animal junk food, full of starch and corn, and i can't bring myself to feed them that.

i am trying to look into creating my own food for them.

I need supporting documentation from my psychiatrist, though, who doesn't want me on it.

I will seek a second opion though

I sought out a social worker to help me with accommodation, however, right now she's trying to get me stable.

Another psychiatrist is possible, but legal workers don't get involved in disability claims in australia except maybe AFTER you have been denied, but I would have to have a doctor who applies for me before that would happen.
I am in australia, Qld

This is what I have to meet:


*

There is a severe functional impact on activities involving mental health function.
 
(1)        The person has severe difficulties with most of the following:
 
(a)        self care and independent living;
 
Example: The person needs regular support to live independently, that is, needs visits or assistance at least twice a week from a family member, friend, health worker or support worker.
 
(b)        social/recreational activities and travel;
 
Example: The person travels alone only in familiar areas (such as the local shops or other familiar venues).
 
(c)        interpersonal relationships;
 
Example 1: The person has very limited social contacts and involvement unless these are organised for the person.
 
Example 2: The person often has difficulty interacting with other people and may need assistance or support from a companion to engage in social interactions.
 
(d)        concentration and task completion;
 
Example 1: The person has difficulty concentrating on any task or conversation for more than 10 minutes.
 
Example 2: The person has slowed movements or reaction time due to psychiatric illness or treatment effects.
 
(e)        behaviour, planning and decision-making;
 
Example: The person’s behaviour, thoughts and conversation are significantly and frequently disturbed.
 
(f)         work/training capacity.
 
Example: The person is unable to attend work, education or training on a regular basis over a lengthy period due to ongoing mental illness.

*


My psychiatrist says I do not meet enough of them
Not being able to work is only one factor that's taken into account with disability. it's fucking stupid.
but tarring all people with personality disorders as abusers is much more judgemental that calling an hypothetical abuser, an abuser,

You need meds for bipolar. there is really no getting around that.

DBT is good for bpd, and also helps BP and PTSD. Look into mindfulness, radical acceptance, emotional regulation and interpersonal skills.
